questions.q: How do you read a parent Account's Industry field from a Contact query?
options: `SELECT Name, Account.Industry FROM Contact`
`SELECT Name, (SELECT Industry FROM Account) FROM Contact`
`SELECT Name, Account_Industry__r FROM Contact`
You must run a second, separate query against Account
questions.explain: Child-to-parent traversal uses dot notation directly in the field list and WHERE clause: Account.Industry.

questions.q: What syntax pulls an Account's related Contacts in the same query as the Account?
options: `SELECT Name, Contacts.Name FROM Account`
`SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account`
`SELECT Name FROM Account JOIN Contact`
`SELECT Name, Contact__r.LastName FROM Account`
questions.explain: Parent-to-child traversal nests a subquery inside the outer SELECT list, e.g. (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts).

questions.q: For a custom object's parent-to-child subquery, what suffix does the child relationship name use?
options: `__child`
No suffix — the object's API name is used as-is
questions.explain: Custom relationship names use __r for both dot-notation child-to-parent access and parent-to-child subquery relationship names.

questions.q: In `[SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account]`, how do you access the nested results for a given Account record `a`?
options: `a.Contacts`, which gives a List<Contact> of the matched subquery rows
`a.get('Contacts')` only, since nested results aren't typed
A second query is still required to get the contacts
`a.Contact__r`
questions.explain: Accessing the child relationship name (Contacts) on the parent record returns a List<Contact> containing the subquery's matches.

questions.q: Can a subquery in a parent-to-child query have its own WHERE clause, independent of the outer query's filter?
options: No, subqueries can only filter on the same conditions as the outer query
Yes — the subquery is itself a query and can filter the children independently
Only if the child object is a custom object
Only if the outer query has no WHERE clause of its own
questions.explain: A subquery can carry its own WHERE clause, letting you filter the nested child records separately from the outer query's filter.
